briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 27, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Direct Domestic and International Impacts
sections.content: Domestically, over the past 45 years, the duration of heatwaves has increased by 39 days, with heatwaves tending to start earlier and end later [5]. Damage to aquaculture farms due to high-temperature climate change and the diversification of agricultural disasters are emerging as serious issues [6, 8]. A Nepalese glacier expert also warned of the severity of natural disasters, pointing out that climate change significantly impacts the occurrence of landslides and debris flows [9]. Internationally, there is a growing call to recognize the reality of climate change through the memory of Hurricane Helen [36], and reports that climate change is even altering the world's finest gourmet menus demonstrate its deep penetration into daily life [39]. These phenomena clearly show that the climate crisis is accelerating globally, emphasizing the need for immediate action.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Adaptation Efforts and Agricultural Transformation
sections.content: To address the direct damages from climate change, reforms to the aquaculture disaster insurance system are being pursued domestically, and specific revision plans are expected to be prepared to minimize damage to aquaculture farms caused by high-temperature climate change [2, 4, 6, 7, 10]. Meanwhile, with agriculture's share of GDP having significantly decreased from 49% in the past to 1.6% currently, there is an argument that climate change and AI should be embraced as new opportunities [3]. The necessity of redesigning prevention systems to prepare for the diversifying agricultural disasters due to climate change is also being emphasized [8]. These are considered important domestic adaptation efforts to strengthen resilience to climate change and build a sustainable society.

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Carbon Neutrality Practices and Trends in Renewable Energy Expansion
sections.content: Efforts to practice carbon neutrality are active across the country. Yongin Special City and Okcheon County are encouraging participation in the 'Carbon Neutrality Point for Vehicles' and 'Carbon Neutrality Point System' [11, 13, 15, 16], while Yangju City is holding a 'Green City Drawing Contest' for children to raise carbon neutrality awareness among future generations [14]. Citizen participation is expanding, with organizations like the Inje Rotary Club practicing carbon neutrality in daily life through environmental cleanup activities [17]. In the energy sector, the outline of the power source composition for the 12th Basic Plan for Long-term Electricity Supply and Demand is emerging, showing efforts to secure both carbon neutrality and power stability [12]. KEPCO E&C is accelerating renewable energy project development in cooperation with Truston Asset Management [23]. Truston Asset Management is investing in the Sinan wind power plant and pursuing repowering, and Gurye County is exploring public development solutions for renewable energy [27, 28], indicating continued concrete movements towards renewable energy expansion.

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges of Renewable Energy Transition and Call for International Climate Action
sections.content: Challenges still abound in the transition to renewable energy. A fire occurred at a new and renewable energy plant in Chungnam [19], and the case where an oversupply of new and renewable energy led to the shutdown of a nuclear power plant, resulting in a loss of 103.2 billion KRW [21], demonstrates the difficulties of energy system integration. Furthermore, financial hurdles, such as financial institutions demanding lump-sum loan repayments after solar panel installation, are hindering the spread of renewable energy [26]. Cheonan City's indiscriminate installation of banners, which contradicts carbon neutrality policies, is causing public concern [18]. Internationally, resistant movements against climate action are observed, such as the significant relaxation of U.S. vehicle fuel efficiency regulations [33] and attempts in Texas to prevent students from learning about climate change [35]. However, international cooperation continues, with the construction of MW-class solar power plants in Tajikistan, which suffers from power shortages, and the completion of ODA projects between Korea and Tajikistan [20, 24, 30]. The voices of island nations struggling with climate change, continuing their fight, and St. Kitts urging global emergency action [38, 41] once again emphasize the urgency of climate action.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, various domestic and international response efforts, and the challenges that still need to be addressed. This is a time when sustained attention and cooperation on climate change are becoming even more crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: Researchers from India and the United States have devised a novel concrete manufacturing method incorporating 10% human waste in biochar form. This concrete has demonstrated a 21% increase in compressive strength and a 42% increase in flexural strength.
summary.cause: This manufacturing method, which replaces a portion of cement with human waste, appears to be effective because the numerous pores in the human waste biochar store moisture, thereby strengthening the concrete.
summary.outlook: This approach could lead to a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by decreasing cement consumption.
